<timestamp>Thursday, Nov 19, 2026, 4:41 PM (UTC-8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
can I export my entire session history and upload it to the github in a folder? I want that folder to have all my teammates session uploads as well
</user_query>
You can share session history on GitHub, but each person’s chats live on their own machine. I’ll check how Cursor stores sessions here and what a shared folder would actually contain.

input.command: git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>$null; git remote -v; git status -sb

content.text:
Yes. Cursor keeps each person’s chats only on that person’s computer, so a shared GitHub folder works if everyone uploads their own history into their own subfolder.

This project already pushes to `https://github.com/vihaanbussa/waypoint-hackathon.git`. Your chats for this workspace are local JSONL files under Cursor’s project data, not in the repo. There are 10 sessions here. GitHub will not pull your teammates’ chats for you.

Use one folder, one subfolder per person:

```text
sessions/
  abhiram/
    <chat-id>.jsonl
  teammate-name/
    <chat-id>.jsonl
```

Each person copies their transcripts into their subfolder, commits, and pushes. Git merges those folders, so the repo ends up with everyone’s uploads.

Two limits:

- A teammate has to do this from their own machine. You cannot export their Cursor history from yours.
- These files are the full chat, including prompts, file contents, and tool output. Anything sensitive that showed up in a chat (keys, account data, student records) would go to GitHub with it. Skim them before the first push.

If you want, I can copy your 10 sessions into `sessions/abhiram/` and commit them. I will not push until you say so.
